subject: Discovery recap: inference cost & performance for Acme Health
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost & performance for Acme Health

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have shared context and clear next steps. Feel free to correct anything I got wrong.

Key pain points you called out:
- Unit economics: inference cost per API call is driving margin pressure for your CareOps product. High volume & long-context prompts are the main concern.
- Latency SLOs: real-time routing for clinician workflows needs <250ms p95 for short prompts.
- Operational predictability: billing spikes from batch jobs and peak hours are causing cost overruns and surprise invoices.

Current stack & constraints:
- Model choice: currently using a mix of hosted LLMs for prototyping + an on-prem model for PHI workloads.
- Infra: Kubernetes cluster with GPU nodes for on-prem; cloud usage through a procurement contract.
- Privacy: PHI must remain on-prem for specific workflows; other inference can be hosted.

Success criteria you listed:
1) Reduce per-token inference cost by at least 40% while maintaining comparable answer quality for triage prompts.
2) Meet latency requirement for clinician-facing flows (p95 <250ms) at 50 req/s.
3) Predictable billing with visibility to cost drivers and capacity planning.

Technical notes / Redwood approaches we discussed that map to your needs:
- Batching & KV caching for repeated prefixes to cut token compute on triage flows.
- Quantization-friendly model variants — willing to run evals to validate quality/latency tradeoffs.
- Smart routing: route PHI traffic to your on-prem deployment and non-PHI traffic to hosted/dedicated pools.
- Dedicated capacity option (reserved) if you want predictable throughput and committed pricing.

Next steps (owners & timing):
- Jordan / Acme: confirm sample traffic pattern + a small set of representative prompts for us to run a cost/quality simulation (by EOD Mon 2/16).
- Dev (me): run a quick sim using your sample prompts (batching and caching on/off) and share a short one-pager with projected unit costs and latency estimates (by Wed 2/18). Attached the Redwood pricing sheet and a benchmark template you can fill.
- Lauren: follow up with a short SOW template and options for Dedicated vs Hosted runbooks (internal).

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (pricing overview), benchmark-summary.csv (traffic template)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow if helpful.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost & performance for Acme Health

Thanks Dev — this is super helpful and accurate. A few clarifications and notes from our side: 

Clarifications:
- The 50 req/s is for the clinician-facing triage microservice only; we also have an async batch job that runs nightly (~30k prompts) where latency is not critical but cost absolutely is.
- For PHI: we need a strict boundary. That boundary is enforced at the request level and must route only to our on-prem stack.

Openness to approaches:
- Quantization: our infra team is open to 8-bit/4-bit quantized models for the batch job if quality is acceptable; clinician-facing flows should start with higher-precision and we can evaluate quality tradeoffs.
- Batching/caching: we definitely want to enable server-side caching for repeated prefixes and are open to Redwood helping tune cache TTLs.

Deliverables for next week:
- I'll upload a CSV of 200 representative prompts (both triage and batch) to the Drive link you shared by end of day Monday.
- Would like the quick sim you mentioned and a short summary that maps cost savings to quantization and batching options.

Also, can you include a high-level estimate of engineering effort on our side for a minimal integration (routing + auth + SSO integration)? Rough ballpark (SWE-days) is fine for now.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Health
j.smith@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199
